correctness.rationale: For every m>=1 and Boolean h, Fourier character conjugation identifies the matrix rank with nonzero ambiguities. Explicit shift/modulation cases give D+1, D/2+2 and D/2+1+s_v counts; adding them yields the formula. Every derivative has one nonzero Walsh coefficient iff it is affine, equivalent to deg(h)<=2, and the cubic derivative has polar rank exactly two in 7*2^(m-3) directions. The packaged independent integer checker verifies 292 cases, without being used as the infinite proof.
